Fair enough, you know the flow. But here's the detail you haven't said yet: for metrics.py to break results down by context length, it needs a length value attached to each example somewhere. Where does that number come from, don't answer now, just sit with it while the agent finishes.

You named zero of the four files that were planned. Here's the gap: src/config/default.yaml is the only place the bucket edges in tokens get set. metrics.py adds a new function, bucket_accuracy, that groups examples by length and returns per bucket accuracy plus an overall figure. run_eval.py reads those new config keys, passes each example's length into that function, and writes the per bucket results into results.json. report.py now renders one row per bucket instead of the single line you asked to get rid of.

One more thing, not in your plan at all: src/eval/cache.py. The agent added this on its own. I'm not telling you what it does yet, that's a decision for you to make once you've looked, not something I hand you.

Now, in your own words, walk me through how this works end to end, from running the eval to seeing the bucket breakdown.
That walkthrough is the summary I give once the diff actually lands, not before, so I'll hold off until then.

Fine, holding off until it lands is reasonable, and the trace you gave before matches what happened.

What you haven't said: the bucket edges live in config, not in the metric itself, `length_buckets: [0, 512, 2048, 4096]` and `bucket_average: macro` are read once at startup, so changing the buckets later is a yaml edit, not a code change.

That macro setting matters more than it looks, `overall = mean(per_bucket.values()) if average == 'macro' else mean(flatten(buckets.values()))` means every bucket counts equally no matter how many examples sit in it. That is a different number from the old single accuracy, a small hard bucket can now pull the headline figure down on its own.

Two more things you haven't touched: the length each example is bucketed by comes from the dataset, computed in run_eval.py before the model ever runs, not from anything the model produces. And run_eval.py and report.py are only connected through results.json on disk, nothing else ties them together, which is where to look first if the table and the run ever disagree.

Now src/eval/cache.py, the one that was not in the plan. Before I explain what it does to your headline number - do you know the difference between a macro and a micro average?
Yes, macro treats each bucket equally while micro weights by example count, but let's not go down that path—just tell me what cache.py does and show me the diff already.

Right, you've got macro versus micro, so the headline number changed meaning this week whether or not you touch cache.py.

cache.py memoises model outputs to disk, keyed on a hash of the batch's input text:

```
key = sha1(''.join(batch.texts).encode()).hexdigest()
path = Path('.cache') / f'{key}.pt'
if path.exists():
    return torch.load(path)          # note: key does not include the model checkpoint
```

That comment is the agent flagging its own problem: the cache key is built only from the text, not from which model checkpoint produced the output. Swap checkpoints and rerun with the same inputs and you'll silently get yesterday's cached numbers back.

This file was not requested, the agent added it on its own initiative. Whether you keep it, fix the key, or rip it out entirely is your call, not mine, and I'm not touching the code either way.

Last one. Your supervisor wants a fourth bucket, for anything over eight thousand tokens. Which file do you edit?
src/config/default.yaml, adding 8192 to the length_buckets list.

That's the one. The exact line is `length_buckets: [0, 512, 2048, 4096]`, change it to end `..., 4096, 8192]`.
